The results show that these bodies are not merely oversight agencies, as they directly influence early childhood education policies, as co-administrators (Hoffmann and Bentes 2008) or fixers (Bardach 1977; Sabatier and Mazmanian 1993; Weimer and Vining 2017) of their implementation by municipalities. It was also found that these accountability institutions have been assuming new responsibilities in the area of education since the 2000s, within an incremental development trajectory (Mahoney and Thelen 2009) marked by a variety of actions, including interinstitutional cooperation.

There are many challenges in minimizing the gaps between scientific evidence and better health outcomes. Knowledge translation (KT) is the movement that knowledge undergoes within an organizational context toward its effective application. The objective of this study was to analyze the occurrence of KT in the Executive Secretariat of Health Surveillance of Pernambuco (SEVS/PE), taking as its object ten evaluative studies on Health Surveillance programs, produced in the Master's Program in Health Evaluation of the Instituto de Medicina Integral Prof. Fernando Figueira, from 2011 to 2015. To this end, a semi-structured interview guide was used, involving seven managers and ten technicians of SEVS-PE. In the analysis of this qualitative case study, a KT model was used, overlaid with a theoretical framework of evaluation use and influence. In eight of the studies analyzed, evidence was categorized into five KT phases. Only the stage of evaluating the use of knowledge was not evidenced. Different types of use, dimensions, and levels of influence of the evaluations were reported. Among the changes that occurred, the following were reported: creation of new agendas, development of protocols, changes in work processes, establishment of new workflows, and hiring of new professionals.

This article analyzes road safety on federal highways located in urban areas in the Southern region of Brazil. It seeks to evaluate the occurrence of victims, based on records from the Federal Highway Police (PRF), together with pavement, road geometry, and traffic signage conditions, according to the methodology of the National Confederation of Transport (CNT). Critical urban stretches were highlighted using a geoprocessing program, and, for the delimitation of crashes, concepts based on the Safe System approach were used, which holds that traffic crashes, when they occur, should not cause serious or fatal injuries. When deaths and victims with serious injuries are taken into account, the urban stretches of federal highways in the Southern region were among the most dangerous in Brazil. Most highways in urban areas were classified as "good" with regard to their state of conservation, but several segments concentrated a large number of victims, mainly motorcyclists. As a negative highlight, São José, in Santa Catarina, had the most critical stretch. Of the segments with high crash rates, almost all were close to large urban agglomerations or regional capitals, probably due to the large number of trips generated by socioeconomic activities.

The Cactaceae family includes 1,850 species distributed primarily in the Americas, with Brazil being the third largest center of diversity of the family, with 277 species. In this latter center of diversity, the Boa Nova National Park (PNBN), located in the east of the State of Bahia, Brazil, has an area of about 12,065 ha, including an east-west ecotone, with areas of Atlantic Forest being replaced by vine forest (mata-de-cipó) and, farther west, by Caatinga. As part of the 2011 National Action Plan for the conservation of Cactaceae, this work presents the taxonomic study of Cactaceae occurring in the PNBN, and aims to expand knowledge of the local flora and of the Conservation Units of the State of Bahia. The material was collected during four collecting expeditions over one year, along random trails covering the various environments of the park. Ten genera and 15 species were recorded: Arrojadoa penicillata, Brasilicereus phaeacanthus, Brasiliopuntia brasiliensis, Cereus jamacaru, Cereus sp., Melocactus ernestii, Pereskia aculeata, P. bahiensis, Pilosocereus catingicola, P. pentaedrophorus subsp. robustus, Rhipsalis hileiabaiana, R. russellii, Stephanocereus leucostele, Tacinga funalis, and T. werneri. Within the PNBN, the vine forest (mata-de-cipó) and Caatinga vegetation presented the highest numbers of species, with eight and five species, respectively, while the Atlantic Forest presented a single species.

This article proposes an analysis of the issue of disease and death in artistic representations in painting collections in Belém do Pará between the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries. To this end, it proposes a cross-cutting reading based on questions posed in the present, during the covid-19 pandemic, as a comparative heuristic resource. It therefore seeks to establish a dialogue between present and past through images, potencies, reverberations, discursive records, and museum exhibitions. Thus, diseases portrayed in painting, such as cancer and tuberculosis, seen in the context of the epidemics of the belle époque, are now analyzed not only within the framework of the comorbidities of the present-day pandemic, but also as a cognitive repertoire of the very history and memory of images in the Amazon.

Considering the particleboard industry, most of it uses synthetic adhesives, especially urea-formaldehyde-based ones, and in this sense, studies that encompass the characteristics of alternative materials for the panel industry become important, especially when considering the final cost of the products. The general objective of this study was to evaluate changes in the chemical structure of the adhesive that could cause possible modifications in its binding properties as a function of replacing the urea-formaldehyde adhesive with lignosulfonate. To this end, the elemental chemical composition of lignosulfonate and its chemical bonds were determined by infrared (IR) spectroscopy and nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), both pure and in composition with different catalysts; the properties of urea-formaldehyde and its modifications, such as pH, viscosity, and gel time, were also determined. The NMR analysis showed, for lignosulfonate, the same pattern generally obtained for lignin derivatives in terms of chemical bonds. The elemental chemical analysis showed high contents of Mg, Ca, and Na. The addition of lignosulfonate to urea-formaldehyde caused acidification of the adhesive and a reduction in viscosity values. The effect on gel time was also affected; however, it was found that the methodology for this type of polymer should be adapted relative to the traditional method, by subjecting it to a temperature above 90°C. The results led to the conclusion that it is possible to use lignosulfonate as a replacement for urea-formaldehyde adhesive in particleboard.

The aim of this paper is to highlight the possible role of student exchange agencies as facilitators of immigration. In order to understand the consumption behavior and the factors that motivate Brazilians to immigrate to Australia, the researchers conducted a survey with 608 consumers, affiliated with 10 Facebook groups representing communities of Brazilians in Australia. Using a logistic regression model, the researchers defined the dependent variable of the study as the permanent immigrant, assigned the value 0 (zero) if respondents did not intend to live in Australia permanently, or 1 (one) otherwise. The independent variables, representing factors present at the time of their arrival in the country that may affect the decision to immigrate permanently, were gender, age at arrival, future intention to start a business, student visa, and educational level. The results point to statistically significant factors related to immigration to Australia, based on the respondents' sociodemographic profiles. In-depth interviews were also conducted with a travel agent and Brazilian residents. As practical implications, the paper highlights consumption behavior, motivations for immigration, and the factors that lead people to hire student exchange agencies.

Although Araliaceae has many species with leaves bearing toothed margins, the anatomical structure of these projections has never been investigated. Thus, this study aimed to characterize the anatomy of the leaf teeth of Hydrocotyle asterias Cham. & Schltdl., a representative of this family. Fragments of the leaf blade with marginal teeth were processed according to standard techniques for light microscopy (clearing, paradermal sections, and histochemical tests) and scanning electron microscopy. The teeth of H. asterias consist of hydathodes, whose size, shape, and spacing between teeth vary across the different stages of leaf development. They have a uniseriate epidermis composed of isodiametric cells with slightly thickened walls, a thin cuticle, and stomata concentrated in the apical region. The vascularization consists of xylem that extends up to the epithem. This study presents the first information on the anatomical structure of leaf teeth in the family Araliaceae and expands knowledge about hydathodes located on leaf teeth.

The present study highlights the trajectories of 19 Brazilian entrepreneurs of startups established in Canada. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews with the respondents. Given that there are few studies on Brazilian entrepreneurs in Canada, we sought to determine the barriers and main difficulties they face, as well as the opportunities and success strategies they have pursued in the country. The paper begins with a discussion of immigrant entrepreneurship and startup creation. It then addresses the migratory movement of Brazilians to Canada, covering Brazilian businesses in general and startups, also focusing on the definition of startups and their profile in Brazil, in addition to the Canadian startup ecosystem. The theoretical contribution of this paper is to compare the collected data with theories of immigrant entrepreneurship, effectuation theory applied to startups, and the Uppsala model, aiming to theoretically list the elements observed in the group studied. At the end of the paper, a diagram is presented that illustrates the immigrant entrepreneur's journey in the process of designing and validating their business model, and the conclusions may contribute to entrepreneurship theories by showing specific aspects of the Canadian startup context. As for practical implications, the study can provide data for possible future policies aimed at attracting more qualified and skilled Brazilian entrepreneurs to the Canadian technology ecosystem.

The objective of this study was to estimate the potential for soil loss using the Universal Soil Loss Equation and to identify the factors that control the erosive process in a hillslope watershed. The rainfall erosivity factor (R) was calculated from normal precipitation data, thus obtaining monthly erosion indices. The soil erodibility factor (K) was obtained from soil sampling carried out on a grid of 340 points, whose values were interpolated by the ordinary kriging method. The topographic factor (LS) was generated from the Digital Elevation Model (DEM), while the land use and management and conservation practice factors (CP) were obtained through field observations and tabulated values. The highest loss rates cover 27% of the area and are concentrated in locations with steeper slopes where shallow soils predominate, such as Lithic Neosols and Regolithic Neosols. The LS factor determined the magnitude of the erosive process, and the CP factor showed the strongest relationship with the control of soil losses. The results show the importance of the soil cover factor, indicating that vegetation maintenance measures and conservation practices should be adopted and considered by environmental managers in hillslope regions with a predominance of shallow soils associated with steep relief.

The present study presents an application of the WRF mesoscale model to the simulation of an intense and persistent wind episode that occurs with irregular frequency at the Guapé reservoir, in the state of Minas Gerais, Brazil. This event alters the routine of the population in the region, causing, for example, the vessel that makes the crossing between the cities of Guapé and Capitólio to suspend its service. During one of these episodes, which occurred on September 22, 2016, measurements were made using a Zephir ZP300 LIDAR and an anemometric tower, and these data were subsequently used to validate the simulations. To evaluate the results, simulated and observed pressure, temperature, humidity, and wind speed were compared. The analysis of the simulated vertical velocity profiles suggests the presence of a low-level jet, located at around 500 m above the surface, generated by a post-frontal temperature gradient, whose lower portion would have been accelerated by the terrain and by the variation in land-water surface roughness. Further studies are currently under way so that some type of preventive action can be suggested to the population and local authorities.

This paper analyzes the multiple dimensions of the work of street-level bureaucrats in the Brazilian context of public policy implementation. The aim of this essay is to contribute to a better understanding of the topic through an expanded analytical approach. To this end, a literature search was carried out in academic digital databases, which made it possible to identify and select national and international works according to methodologically defined criteria. The publications obtained were analyzed and organized according to the following conceptual categories: discretion, structures, individual action, and relationships. From the tension between rules and discretion in public administration, the analysis and interpretation of these texts showed: a) the need to compare, separately and jointly, three different perspectives on the work of street-level bureaucrats (the structural, the individual action, and the relational perspectives); b) the need to understand how these perspectives are articulated in the implementation process itself. Following this literature review, hypotheses were formulated for an expanded analysis of the work of implementing bureaucrats, outlining directions for future research on the topic. This essay contributes to the debate on the subject with a novel theoretical construct that seeks to integrate the three different analytical perspectives presented in a dialectical synthesis of the central concepts of the literature on public policy implementation by street-level bureaucrats.

Bacterial pustule, caused by the bacterium Xanthomonas axonopodis pv. glycines, is considered one of the most serious bacterial diseases in soybean. The objective of this work was to develop and validate a diagrammatic scale for assessing the severity of bacterial pustule in soybean. To develop the scale, soybean leaflets with different levels of severity were collected, thereby determining the maximum and minimum values of disease amount, and the intermediate severity levels of the scale were established according to the Weber-Fechner law of visual stimulus. The values proposed for the scale were: 1.4%; 3%; 6%; 9%; 20%, and 29.5%. To validate the scale, eight raters with no experience in assessing the disease evaluated 39 photographs with different severity levels, with and without the aid of the scale. The severity estimates given by the raters were compared with the actual severity values (determined with Assess 2.0 software from digital images of leaves with symptoms) and subjected to simple linear regressions to evaluate the raters' accuracy. The raters' precision was determined through the coefficients of determination and the variance of absolute errors. Estimates made using the proposed diagrammatic scale resulted in a significant increase in the coefficient of determination and a lower variance of absolute errors, providing greater precision and accuracy of the assessments, and the scale can be adopted for assessing the severity of bacterial pustule in soybean.

The goal is to examine how traces of cinema are woven into the literary threads of "Pela noite" by Caio Fernando Abreu, and why its characters look at the world as if it were cinema. Would these be reflections of the very conversion of the contemporary world into traces of cinema and/or simulacra, which also include other links of the cultural industry? Would they be reflections of an urban experience perceived as moving screens, the result of experiences mediated by glass, windows, and windshields as if they were camera lenses? The novella is the starting point for rethinking how much the cultural industry has altered human behavior, establishing new relationships among the subject, the material world, and the devices designed for the technical reproducibility of images.

One of the alternatives for obtaining potential species for the revegetation of degraded areas is to use those that develop from the topsoil seed bank, and in this context, grasses are the most suitable because they have characteristics associated with soil stabilization. This study aimed to evaluate the native species that developed from a ferruginous topsoil seed bank and to select the grasses with the highest importance value index (IVI), considering them potential species for use in revegetation programs. The topsoil was deposited at Gerdau's Research and Innovation Unit in Ferruginous Rupestrian Fields (Campos Rupestres Ferruginosos), Ouro Branco, MG, Brazil, and after plant germination and establishment, phytosociological studies were carried out. Eragrostis polytricha Nees showed the highest values not only of IVI, but also of Relative Frequency and Relative Cover, and additionally showed the second highest Relative Density value. Therefore, we recommend E. polytricha for use in revegetation programs.

This study aimed to evaluate the effect of a Pinus taeda stand on the floristic composition and structure of the seed bank of a remnant of Araucaria Forest (Mixed Ombrophilous Forest, MOF). To this end, 160 seed bank samples were collected, 80 from a MOF remnant and 80 from a P. taeda stand. The samples were placed to germinate in two separate greenhouses, under 35% and 75% shading levels. A total of 11,669 woody and herbaceous individuals were counted, distributed among 31 botanical families and 84 species. The families Asteraceae and Poaceae were the most representative in herbaceous species richness. Among the woody species, Solanaceae and Asteraceae were the most representative in both areas. The species P. taeda was recorded only in the seed bank of the stand itself. The seed bank of the pine stand was characterized mainly by low woody species richness, which demonstrates its influence on the seed stock. On the other hand, the evaluated MOF remnant does not appear to be influenced by the proximity of the pine stand in terms of its seed bank.

The largest volume of grape juice produced in Brazil comes from the Isabel cultivar. However, blending with other cultivars is necessary to improve juice quality, which increases the demand for other cultivars, especially Bordô. Therefore, the objective of this study was to evaluate the influence of the cultivars BRS Rúbea, BRS Cora, BRS Violeta, BRS Carmem, BRS Magna, and Bordô, in blends with Isabel, on the physicochemical, colorimetric, and sensory characteristics of juices produced in the Vale do Rio do Peixe Region, Santa Catarina State, Brazil. The juices were prepared at Epagri – Videira Experimental Station, Santa Catarina State, as follows: (ISA) 100% Isabel; (ISA+RUB) 70% Isabel + 30% Rúbea; (ISA+COR) 70% Isabel + 30% Cora; (ISA+VIO) 70% Isabel + 30% Violeta; (ISA+CAR) 70% Isabel + 30% Carmem; (ISA+MAG) 70% Isabel + 30% Magna; (ISA+BOR) 70% Isabel + 30% Bordô, and were evaluated for physicochemical composition, colorimetric composition, and sensory profile. The highest titratable acidity was found in ISA+MAG, followed by ISA+BOR. The ISA+VIO juices had the highest mean soluble solids content, differing only from ISA+CAR, which also had the lowest acidity among the treatments. The ISA+VIO and ISA+CAR juices had higher soluble solids content than the 100% Isabel juice. The lowest lightness was observed in the ISA+VIO juices, followed by ISA+CAR. Regarding sensory attributes, significant differences were observed only for color and acidity. The ISA+VIO, ISA+CAR, and ISA+BOR juices received the highest scores for color. All the cultivars tested influenced the colorimetric characteristics of the juice, proving to be alternatives for improving the color of Isabel juices. Sensorially, only color and acidity were influenced by the different blends.

The use of rainwater in buildings is an attractive alternative as a water source. However, to enable its use, rainwater must be treated to reach the required quality. Filters are widely used and come in several models. In order to evaluate different filtration systems, the parameters obtained with each treatment unit surveyed were compared with the values recommended by ABNT (2007). The efficiencies of the systems were also compared with one another. To this end, a literature review was carried out based on a search of the existing literature. The aim was to organize information on the state of the art of rainwater treatment units worldwide and to contribute to the consolidation of the use of these systems. A lack of standardization in methods and parameters was identified, which hinders an accurate analysis of which models would be most suitable for possible usage scenarios. It was also found that the water quality standard required by the Brazilian standard was not met in any case. Nevertheless, the models studied showed promising results, achieving high removal percentages, mostly ranging from 60% to 100%.

This article discusses the adherence of industrial taxonomies from the evolutionary tradition to the reality of Brazilian manufacturing industry, based on the selection of indicators of innovative activities for the year 2014. The data are analyzed using the clustering technique, with 30 indicators grouped into seven different sets of characteristics of innovative activities. The study assumes that the adequacy of these classifications to the Brazilian reality is justified as a relevant research problem, since these taxonomies were originally conceived on the basis of the productive structures of developed economies, requiring adaptations and qualifications in the context of a peripheral economy such as Brazil's, which is also marked by sectoral specificities. The results suggest relative adherence to international patterns in the period analyzed, with occasional discrepancies in some sectors.

The large volume of coal ash accumulated in the storage basins of the Energia Pecém Thermoelectric Power Plant has created a demand for research proposing different ways of using this waste, so as to give this material a final destination. The use of ash in dry covers for waste deposits proved to be a viable alternative, owing to the existence of studies on the subject and the possibility of absorbing a significant amount of the volume of waste produced. The study presented corresponds to the second stage of a research project that verified the feasibility of applying coal ash in cover systems for municipal solid waste landfills. Based on the results of a preliminary numerical modeling, three soil columns were built, representing three cover models: Column A – an upper layer of natural soil (30 cm) and a layer of sealing material consisting of the MS70C30 soil-ash mixture (30 cm, with 70% soil and 30% ash); Column B – a layer of natural soil (30 cm) and a layer of sealing material made of composite ash (30 cm); and Column C – a single layer of natural soil (30 cm), representing the cover found at the Sanitary Landfill of the Municipality of Caucaia. Column A was instrumented with three moisture sensors. Two infiltration tests were carried out in each column, evaluating the percolated volumes in each system and the saturation profiles of the instrumented column (Column A). When evaluating the percolated volume in each test, the MS70C30 mixture (Column A) was found to show the best performance, resulting in a percolated volume far lower than that of the other two models. The material also maintained high saturation conditions, above 90% throughout almost all of the tests, a condition necessary to reduce biogas leakage from inside the system.

The objective of this article is to examine the factors associated with seeking preventive health services among the Brazilian adult population. The sample consisted of participants in the National Health Survey (2013) who reported seeking a health service in the previous 15 days, classified as "treatment/diagnosis" or "preventive." The explanatory variables included sex, age group, skin color, marital status, schooling, household location, private health insurance coverage, and length of enrollment in the Family Health Strategy (FHS). Associations were assessed using prevalence ratios (PR), obtained from the Poisson model, taking into account the complexity of the sampling design. The sample consisted of 32,377 individuals who sought health services, 12.94% of them for "preventive" actions. Seeking this type of care was more frequent among women and less frequent among older individuals, those who did not live with a partner, and those with lower schooling. Not having private health insurance was associated with lower use of prevention. Being enrolled in the FHS was not associated with seeking preventive actions. Despite the efforts and the recognition of the importance of prevention, most individuals still seek health services for treatment.

In this article, we describe and analyze the process of enactment of child and adolescent sexual abuse as a "social problem" to be addressed by the Network for the Care of Children and Adolescents Victims of Sexual Violence of Fortaleza, Ceará (the Network). We observed practices and experiences, whether collective or individual, that mobilize and articulate multiple elements capable of producing "cases of sexual abuse" in a Specialized Reference Center for Social Assistance (CREAS) in the city. The term child and adolescent sexual abuse is grounded in the premise that the union of child and adult sexualities is unacceptable and, therefore, abusive, because the adult's aim is to obtain his or her own sexual pleasure. However, for a situation to be considered child and adolescent sexual abuse in the Network, the sexual situation must be disclosed, reported, analyzed, typified, enumerated, and counted, forming over the course of the care process a dossier with specialized documentary records capable of technically reporting the event.

This article aims to set out the main issues involved in the process of translating from German into Brazilian Portuguese the book Opium für Ovid: Ein Kopfkissenbuch von 22 Frauen (Ópio para Ovídio: um Livro do Travesseiro de 22 mulheres), by Yoko Tawada. With a view to the exercise of translating, this work should be understood as a preliminary study of the writer and her book Opium for Ovid, written in a foreign language. In a context of constant migration and, at the same time, of denial of the Other and xenophobia, the pursuit of an experience of alterity is understood to be necessary. In this sense, this work seeks to shift the gaze toward a foreign perspective and language, so that the translated text affords an experience with the fremd.

The central theme of this text is the discourses on development surrounding the Tripartite Cooperation Program for the Agricultural Development of the Tropical Savannah in Mozambique – ProSavana, a joint cooperation project of the Brazilian, Japanese, and Mozambican governments. The objective is to interpret how the idea of "emptiness" is produced and reinforced in the program's official promotional material, as well as in its Master Plan. As a secondary source, some interviews with key interlocutors were also used. The reflection draws on the theoretical-methodological framework of French-school discourse analysis in dialogue with critical perspectives on development. The analysis points to the (re)production of the idea that the Mozambican savannah is an "empty place," uninhabited and awaiting development, regardless of the people who are there and their own ways of existing in the world. Moreover, although ProSavana is not formally intended as a "sustainable development" program, the imperative to mobilize it as such is evident. However, this appears to be a futile attempt, given the repetition of practices despite the innovation in the predominant discourse, which implies nothing in terms of sustainability.

The incidence of degradation agents on buildings gives rise to degradation mechanisms that lead to the development of anomalies, which reduce the performance of building systems. In this context, investigating the relationship between anomalies, agents, and mechanisms is fundamental to providing support for service life studies and for the development of more durable materials and elements. The objective of this study is to investigate the severity and extent of degradation of mortar-clad facades, identifying patterns that may condition the degradation of this element. This approach is based on the inspection of buildings in use, and for this purpose the Degradation Measurement Method is employed. The methodology is applied to the study of 90 facade samples from buildings aged between 20 and 60 years located in Brasília, Brazil. The analyses are based on degradation indicators, quantified from the variables investigated, specifically solar orientation and facade zones. The results allow the identification of typical degradation patterns. Cracking is the anomaly that most degrades the facades. The top is the facade zone where the greatest severity of degradation occurs. The greatest incidence of degradation, in turn, occurs in the continuous wall zone. The north and south orientations are the most degraded.

In recent years, the agricultural frontier of oil palm in the Amazon region has continued to advance, causing changes in land cover in this region. Given the need to understand the influence of this crop on surface albedo, this study aims to compare the fluctuations in surface albedo in an area of oil palm cultivation with those of pasture, forest, and secondary vegetation. To make this comparison, orbital data were used, based on the MCD43A3 product of the Terra/MODIS satellite for the years 2015 and 2016. The samples selected for the study area showed that oil palm had little variation, with an estimated mean value of α = 0.14, being statistically distinct from the other land uses and covers, with albedo ranked as: Pasture > Oil palm > Secondary vegetation > Forest. This demonstrates that possible conversions from one cover to another may influence the surface radiation balance; that is, if oil palm cultivation continues to advance over pasture areas, this would decrease surface albedo and consequently lead to changes in the microclimate, whereas if the expansion occurs over areas of secondary vegetation or forest, a reversal will occur, which may contribute to climate change.

ASTM A572 Grade 50 steel is used in the manufacture of welded assemblies for wind turbines; for this reason, stress relief is of great importance for correcting the impacts caused by welding processes, as well as for understanding the final properties obtained through this process. The objective of this study is to compare the mechanical properties and residual stresses (hole-drilling method) in ASTM A572 Grade 50 steel samples welded by the submerged arc process, subjected to stress relief in the thermal condition (PWHT) and in the as-welded condition (SST), following the normative requirements of AWS D1.1-2015. The results for the PWHT condition show lower hardness, yield strength, tensile strength, and residual stresses, and higher elongation and impact absorbed energy values than the SST condition. Both conditions passed the side bend test. The results obtained demonstrate the importance of the stress relief process, which minimizes the undesirable effects of welding processes on components.

The objective of this study was to verify the influence of supplementation with different combinations of organic minerals on performance and carcass characteristics, as well as to evaluate its economic viability, for finishing pigs. Eighty-eight castrated males were used, divided among four treatments: a control with a basal diet and supplementation with CrFe, MgSe, and CrFeMgSe, during the 28 days prior to slaughter. The experimental design was a randomized block design, with the experimental unit represented by two animals. Animals supplemented with CrFeMgSe showed worse final weight, average daily gain, and feed intake throughout the period, with a consequent reduction in carcass weight, lower loin depth, smaller loin eye area, and a lower amount of lean meat in the carcass. There was an increase in diet cost for the CrFe, MgSe, and CrFeMgSe groups, respectively. The use of chromium plus iron and magnesium plus selenium, combined in pairs, does not alter performance parameters or carcass characteristics. The combination of the four minerals, however, worsens these characteristics and increases diet cost.

Meteorological conditions unfavorable to pollutant dispersion, together with high atmospheric pollutant emission rates and complex topography, frequently favor the occurrence of high pollutant concentrations in the Metropolitan Region of Rio de Janeiro (MRRJ). In this context, this study examined the influence of meteorological conditions in two periods in which high concentrations of O3 and PM10 occurred on consecutive days in the MRRJ. The study used the Weather Research and Forecasting Model (WRF), a mesoscale numerical model, to simulate the meteorological conditions and variables favorable to the persistence of these episodes, examining the influence of the South Atlantic Subtropical Anticyclone (SASA), high air temperatures, low wind speeds, and absence of cloud cover, in agreement with the observed data. Visual analysis showed that the model was effective in representing the SASA, precipitation, and cloud cover. The model showed a positive Pearson linear correlation between simulated and observed temperature above 0.71 in both periods at all 8 meteorological stations, and a positive Pearson linear correlation between simulated and observed relative humidity above 0.72. The mean error (ME) calculation indicated that, in general, the model underestimated air temperature and overestimated relative humidity. The application of statistical methods to the observed and simulated data showed that the model has skill in representing the meteorological variables for most of the stations.

Introduction: The identification of complications of primary palatoplasty may vary among professionals from different health areas due to the lack of standardization in fistula classification. This study aimed to verify the consensus between plastic surgery (PS) and speech-language pathology (SLP) professionals regarding the occurrence of fistula, as reported at the same craniofacial service. Methods: An analysis was performed of the records of the PS and SLP areas regarding the presence and location of fistulas, as reported in 466 medical records of patients with a history of unilateral complete cleft lip and palate. To compare the findings between both areas, a gold standard verification of fistula occurrence (FO) was established by an experienced plastic surgeon. Results: The PS area reported that 25% of the 466 patients had a fistula, compared with 37% reported by SLP, while FO indicated a fistula in 35% of cases. Kappa statistics revealed fair agreement between FO and PS (r=0.32) and substantial agreement between FO and SLP (r=0.63). Conclusion: Disagreement was observed between the speech-language pathology and plastic surgery areas regarding the occurrence and location of fistula after primary palatoplasty at the same craniofacial center. The data point to the need to create and implement a standardized fistula classification system that can be used effectively by craniofacial teams, favoring scientific evidence on cleft lip and palate treatment outcomes.

Statistics show that, worldwide, women are the main providers of human life reproduction work, which involves household and care tasks, defined as unpaid work. Its value and importance to society must be recognized. One way of doing this is to show the volume of wealth, in the form of goods and services, generated by this invisible work, through its measurement/valuation. To this end, it is necessary to create a Satellite Account for unpaid work, fulfilling one of the objectives proposed by the UN in its list of Millennium Goals. Accordingly, this study proposes a discussion of a social indicator of unpaid work for Brazil to be incorporated into the National Accounts. This paper discusses the meaning of Satellite Accounts for gender statistics, highlighting the economic importance of household chores and care work, not only for families but for society as a whole, and emphasizing the difficulties in reconciling work and family for those responsible for unpaid work. Finally, the text develops a methodological proposal to estimate unpaid work in Brazil that is compatible with the national accounts methodology.

Cassava black rot caused by Scytalidium lignicola has become an important disease in producing states due to large production losses. Therefore, the objective of the present study was to evaluate the effect of sources and doses of organic matter, alone and added to sandy soil, on the suppressiveness of mycelial growth of S. lignicola CMM 1098. Two experiments were carried out: the first aimed to evaluate the effect of extracts of organic materials (poultry litter, goat manure, cattle manure, and earthworm humus) incorporated into potato dextrose agar (PDA) culture medium at concentrations of 10, 20, 30, and 40% (v/v), and the second evaluated the effect of the organic materials mixed with sandy soil, using the same sources and doses. Poultry litter was the most efficient source in inhibiting the mycelial growth of S. lignicola at a 40% dose, with a mycelial growth inhibition of 69.75% only when the extracts were not autoclaved. Non-autoclaved poultry litter at doses equal to or greater than 30% was effective in suppressing the mycelial growth of S. lignicola CMM 1098. Non-autoclaved sandy soil with added sources and doses of organic matter is highly efficient in suppressing the growth of S. lignicola CMM 1098.

In this study, the microstructure and intergranular corrosion resistance of ferritic stainless steels with additions of Nb, Ti, and (Ti+Nb) subjected to TIG welding were investigated. The structural characterization of the weld beads was carried out by optical microscopy (OM), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS). Susceptibility to sensitization was evaluated qualitatively through Practice W of the ASTM A763 standard and quantitatively through the DL-EPR technique. A martensite network was observed at the grain boundaries in the weld region of the unstabilized steel, and a completely ferritic microstructure was observed in the samples of steels with stabilizer additions. Practice W revealed generalized corrosion inside the grains of AISI 430 steel and the presence of ditches in AISI 430 Ti; concomitantly, the DL-EPR technique showed that these steels were sensitized by welding. In contrast, the samples of steels with additions of Nb and (Ti+Nb) maintained good corrosion resistance, remaining free of sensitization after welding.

The present study aims to analyze Primary Health Care (PHC) as a learning environment for medical students. A descriptive cross-sectional study with a qualitative approach was carried out through four focus groups with interns from the four medical schools in Fortaleza (Ceará, Brazil). The method of interpretation of meanings was used, and two empirical categories were identified. For the students, Primary Care is an important teaching setting for correlating theory and practice, but without recognizing its importance within the Unified Health System (SUS). Thus, the defense of the SUS is not included as an important principle of their profession. However, incentives for teaching in Primary Care and the development of humanistic aspects during training would be motivating factors for working in this area.

In critical situations resulting from low hydroelectric reservoir levels, the control of the Brazilian electric sector is based on hydrothermal planning that depends on future inflows to hydroelectric power plants (HPPs). Hydrological uncertainties are considered through synthetic scenarios of sequences of natural inflow energies to the subregions. Two computational models are used to optimize the system: NEWAVE (medium and long term) and DECOMP (short term). NEWAVE is an energy planning model applied to the National Interconnected System (SIN) that uses Stochastic Dual Dynamic Programming (SDDP) to determine the operating policy that minimizes the marginal cost of operation over a horizon of up to 5 years. The objective of this work is to evaluate the performance of NEWAVE, through the NWLISTOP functionality, in projecting Natural Inflow Energy (NIE) and Stored Energy (SE) in the Northeast (NE) Subsystem for the years 2012 to 2016. It was found that the model tends to overestimate the NIE and SE values. The results indicate the need for techniques that allow the optimization of long-term operation planning, especially in episodes of extreme drought.

The semiarid region of the State of Rio Grande do Norte can be divided into two main geoenvironmental units: the Sertaneja Depression and the Potiguar Sedimentary Basin. Although the flora of sandy sedimentary basins is usually different from that of crystalline terrains, part of the Potiguar Basin has stony paleo-alluvial deposits with rounded pebbles, imposing different edaphic conditions on the flora. The Açu National Forest is located in a stretch of the edge of the Potiguar Basin with pebble deposits, which make the soil stony. The objective of this study was to characterize the phytosociological structure of the caatinga in the FLONA and its surroundings and to understand the biogeographic links of the local flora in relation to other Caatinga areas. We selected areas within and around the FLONA and sampled 1,500 woody individuals belonging to 33 species. The biogeographic links show that the stony edge of the Potiguar Basin is closer to the flora of crystalline terrains than to the sandy terrains of other sandy sedimentary basins.

This article aims to analyze the content and material aspects of the primer "Viver é lutar" ("To Live Is to Struggle"), published in 1963, which was part of the didactic collection of the same name developed by the Movimento de Educação de Base (MEB, Grassroots Education Movement) as support for adult literacy classes in the context of Brazilian radio schools in the early 1960s, considering the political context of the Brazilian dictatorial regime (1964-1985) and the repression of social movements dedicated to adult education. "O Conjunto Didático 'Viver é lutar'", reports produced by the MEB, and letters written by monitors who took part in the movement were also used as documentary sources. The didactic material shows an effort to bring in elements of the popular culture of the sertão as a didactic-pedagogical strategy to generate identification with the peasants served by the movement, while also taking into account the different intellectual and ideological tendencies in dispute within the Catholic Church that were mobilized in the construction of the material, related to its political, pedagogical, and religious conceptions, which resulted in a distinctive model of peasant education. Finally, we address the process of restructuring the MEB in the context of the dictatorial regime which, according to recent historiography, took place through processes of accommodation to the regime, the consequence of which was the reorganization of its pedagogical principles and the removal of militants from the more radical wings of the movement.

Remote sensing can be used to estimate meteorological data. Using images of atmospheric variables obtained by the AIRS (Atmospheric Infrared Sounder) sensor aboard the Aqua satellite, this study aimed to estimate the daily maximum, minimum, and mean air temperatures in the Federal District region – Brazil. Simple and multiple linear regression models were generated, with surface temperature, relative humidity, and atmospheric water vapor data from the AIRS sensor as explanatory variables, obtained at a twelve-hour temporal scale (daytime and nighttime) during the period from January 2012 to December 2016. Observed air temperature values from two meteorological stations in the studied region were used as dependent variables. The fits showed R² = 0.62 and RMSE = 1.64 °C for maximum temperature data, R² = 0.59 and RMSE = 1.50 °C for minimum temperature data, and R² = 0.76 and RMSE = 1.45 °C for mean temperature data. It is concluded that AIRS sensor data are suitable for monitoring air temperature in the Federal District region.

Yeasts have shown good results in dye biodegradation, making them an environmentally safe and lower-cost alternative for the treatment of effluents containing industrial dyes. Thus, the objective of this work was to study the decolorization of the azo dye Reactive Black 5 (RB5) by the yeast Pichia kudriavzevii SD5. To optimize the decolorization parameters for Reactive Black 5, two experimental designs of the 2³ Central Composite Rotatable Design (CCRD) type were carried out, each design consisting of 17 trials, at 150 rpm for 24 h. The variables studied were pH, temperature, and dye concentration, and the response was the percentage of decolorization. Toxicity tests of the supernatant were also performed after 16 h and 24 h of cultivation, using lettuce seeds (Lactuca sativa) and the microcrustacean Artemia salina. The results showed that P. kudriavzevii SD5 is a yeast tolerant to various types of stress, since it was able to degrade high concentrations of the dye RB5 at 45 °C. However, only temperature had a statistically significant influence (p < 0.05) on the decolorization of RB5. The toxicity bioassays showed that toxicity decreased after 24 h of cultivation, and the absorbance profile of the supernatant pointed to a degradative decolorization mechanism.

This article is a theoretical contribution to the fields of translation studies, postcolonial studies, and African literatures. It takes as its basis the opening of the novel The River Between, by the Kenyan writer Ngugi wa Thiong'o, and some considerations made by scholars such as Edward Said and Conceição Lima, proposing a way of thinking about the relations between native African languages and the languages of the imperial metropoles in African literatures that problematizes the celebration of diasporic hybridities. To this end, it draws on the essays Decolonising the Mind, also by Thiong'o, and "The Politics of Translation" by Gayatri Spivak, in order to develop the image of the "River translation," that is, a place of encounters, transits, and displacements, but also of "afterlife," or fortleben, to use Walter Benjamin's term.

Hydroxyapatite (HAp) is present in the human body in bone and dental tissues, where HAp accounts for 30 to 70% of the total mass of each tissue, and it can be applied as a coating for prostheses or even as a replacement for small bone parts. Thus, the objective was to synthesize HAp by precipitation, incorporate chlorhexidine (CHX), and evaluate its microbial properties. Characterization was performed by XRD, FTIR, TG/DTG, TEM, and SEM. CHX was incorporated into HAp by adsorption, varying the amount incorporated. The diffractogram showed peaks at 25.9°, 31.5°, 32.2°, and 32.7° (2θ), corresponding to the (002), (211), (112), and (300) planes of HAp. The FTIR spectrum showed a band at 1050 cm-1 corresponding to the deformation of phosphate groups and CH2 group deformations at 1485 and 1445 cm-1 of chlorhexidine, which showed porous and cylindrical morphology. The biomaterial showed excellent antimicrobial properties against Streptococcus mutans, Staphylococcus aureus, and Escherichia coli.

More than half of the new HIV infections in 2018 occurred among key populations, including gay men and other men who have sex with men (MSM). Stigma can have a range of behavioral consequences, negatively affecting individuals' lives, and can translate into barriers to accessing public health services. The objective of this article is to analyze the main barriers to access to HIV testing at a Counseling and Testing Center in Curitiba and the linkage of gay men and other MSM to the health service for early treatment. Primary data were collected following a qualitative method, triangulating the techniques of field observation, document analysis, and interviews. The results reveal a lack of trained professionals, difficulty in being welcomed at health services, acceptance of one's sexuality, fear of the result, and lack of information as the main barriers to testing. Difficulty in accepting the diagnosis, prejudice, and discrimination were some of the barriers found to starting treatment. It can be concluded that expanding access to guarantee the rights of those who most struggle to enter the health services of the Unified Health System (SUS) remains a major challenge.

The objective of the study was to evaluate the floristic and structural composition of a stretch of secondary forest in the municipality of Dona Francisca, RS, Brazil. Fifty permanent plots measuring 10 x 20 m were installed systematically, spaced 10 m apart and 40 m between strips, totaling 1 ha. All individuals with a CBH (circumference at breast height) ≥ 15.7 cm were sampled and phytosociological estimators were calculated. A species accumulation curve was constructed to verify sampling sufficiency. To calculate diversity and dominance, the Shannon Index (H') and Pielou's Evenness (J') were used. For potential richness, the nonparametric Jackknife estimators were used. Floristic and structural composition was evaluated using Detrended Correspondence Analysis (DCA). The diameter and hypsometric distributions of the tree community were also verified, as well as the distribution in DBH classes for species with an importance value above 5%. Statistical analyses were performed in the R program. A total of 65 tree and shrub species with 2,045 individuals, distributed in 31 botanical families, were identified. The species with an importance value above 5% were Casearia sylvestris (14.04%), Nectandra lanceolata (12.86%), Cupania vernalis (9.57%), Guarea macrophylla (7.29%), and Ocotea puberula (5.07%). The values for diversity and dominance were, respectively, 2.91 nats.ind-1 and 0.69, indicating that the area has low diversity and dominance by a few species. The DCA shows that the plots are homogeneously distributed across the forest stretch. The diameter distribution was as expected for the tree community, with a tendency toward a reverse J shape, and most trees had heights concentrated in the intermediate stratum of the forest. Of the five species analyzed, only Nectandra lanceolata and Ocotea puberula did not show a negative exponential curve. A predominance of individuals in the first DBH and height classes was observed, which characterizes the resilience of the area after disturbance. It also indicates the fluctuations and stability of the species, in the ecological succession, of a forest at an intermediate stage of regeneration.

Observations were made on the reproductive biology of a recently described species of Rapateaceae (Saxofridericia brasiliensis) in an area of periodically flooded Campina Fechada. During the flowering period, the inflorescences were bagged in order to identify whether the species sets fruit through spontaneous self-pollination. The species has trichomes at the base of the petals that stained with Neutral Red, and its main pollinators are females of nine species of Euglossa, which collect pollen by vibrating the anthers. However, further studies are needed to fully understand the reproductive strategies of the family, given reports of hummingbird pollination in the tribe Schoenocephalieae owing to the presence of nectaries.

This article presents the results of a study on hybrid linguistic norms in New York Times journalistic articles translated into Portuguese and published on the UOL website. According to Faraco (2008) and Bagno (2012), there is a difference between the standard norm (norma padrão) and the cultured norm (norma culta): the former is the set of rules that prescribe linguistic forms to be followed according to an idealized model of language, but which is difficult for most users to follow; the latter is the set of linguistic forms that are actually used by many writers and are therefore more intuitively accessible, although not accepted by the conservative grammatical tradition represented by the standard norm, commonly disseminated in grammar compendiums and style manuals. The aim is to assess whether it is possible to state that journalistic texts translated from English, similarly to what has already been proven to occur with journalistic texts originally written in Portuguese, are equally permeable to linguistic forms not sanctioned by the standard norm.

This essay adopts Foucauldian thought as a basis for proposing a theoretical step back around the notion of the "right to look" as a claim to a position in the struggles over "how to see." After contextualizing the debate, I review two specific texts that engage with Foucault: Can the Subaltern Speak? by Gayatri Spivak, and Necropolitics by Mbembe. From the first, I infer the general idea that the right to look is the opposite of the right to "see without being seen." From the second, I deduce a function of opacity and of management of invisibility that necropolitics exerts in conjunction with biopolitics. Finally, I argue that, if all "seeing" depends on a "not seeing," the right to look claims a position that is always yet to be constructed.
